title: The 100 high-impact verbs (1–50)
blocks: Read the columns as a word family. The real power of this table is not memorising past tenses; it is being able to move across a row. If increase (verb) is overused, slide to an increase (noun) or increasing (adjective) and rebuild the sentence. That flexibility is exactly what Lexical Resource rewards.
**preposition**: preposition that most commonly follows the verb or its noun
**-**: there is no common single-word form in that class, or no fixed preposition
Spelling follows British conventions (analyse, emphasise, utilise), which IELTS accepts and expects.

title: The 100 high-impact verbs (51–100)
blocks: The verb affect has the noun effect, not affect. This is the most examined spelling trap in the language, so read row 5 twice: you affect something (verb), and the effect is the result (noun).

Most rows let you paraphrase by shifting class. “The policy improved education” can become “the policy led to an improvement in education” or “the policy had a beneficial effect on education.” Practise sliding along a row until it is automatic; it is the engine of paraphrase in Chapter 5.

title: The linking word upgrade guide
blocks: Cohesion is scored directly, in the Coherence and Cohesion criterion in Writing and inside Fluency and Coherence in Speaking. Most candidates connect ideas with and, but, so, because, and also. These are not wrong, but a whole script built on them signals Band 6. The fix is a controlled set of higher-level devices, used accurately and not stacked one on top of another.
furthermore, moreover, in addition, additionally, what is more
Renewable energy is clean. Furthermore, it is becoming cheaper each year.
however, nevertheless, in contrast, conversely, on the contrary
The scheme was expensive. Nevertheless, it delivered clear benefits.
notwithstanding, despite this, even so, admittedly, granted that
Notwithstanding the cost, the investment proved worthwhile.
owing to, due to, on account of, as a result of, given that, since
Owing to a shortage of teachers, class sizes have grown.
consequently, therefore, thus, hence, as a result, accordingly
Demand fell sharply; consequently, prices dropped.
Some favour strict rules; conversely, others prefer flexibility.
for instance, to illustrate, namely, such as
Several cities, such as Dhaka and Chittagong, are expanding rapidly.
in conclusion, to sum up, overall, on balance, ultimately
On balance, the advantages outweigh the drawbacks.
“due to” and “owing to” take a noun, not a clause.
Due to the government invested more, education improved.
Owing to greater investment, education improved. / Education improved because the government invested more.
These devices are followed by a noun or noun phrase. If you want a full clause with a subject and verb, use because.
The plan was costly, however, it worked.
The plan was costly. However, it worked. / The plan was costly; however, it worked.
When however joins two complete sentences, it takes a full stop or semicolon before it and a comma after it. A comma alone on both sides creates a comma splice, which is penalised.

One cohesive device per idea is enough. Beginning three sentences in a row with Moreover, Furthermore, In addition is a mechanical overuse that examiners explicitly penalise. Vary the devices, and let some sentences connect through meaning alone. Range means variety, not density.

blocks.title: Exercise 3.1 · Verb Form and Collocation Drill
blocks.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct form of the verb in brackets, or with the correct preposition where a blank has no verb. Use the 100-verb table to check forms and preposition combinations.

items.prompt: Over the past decade, the urban population has ______ (grow) by nearly twenty per cent.
items.reason: present perfect needs has + V3; grow is irregular (grew, grown).

items.prompt: If food prices continue ______ (rise), many families will struggle.
items.reason: continue accepts both the infinitive and the -ing form.

items.prompt: Rural households often depend ______ agriculture for their entire income.
items.reason: depend on is the fixed collocation.

items.prompt: Many students benefit ______ free online learning resources.
items.reason: benefit from.

items.prompt: Between 2000 and 2010, car sales ______ (peak) at forty thousand units.
items.reason: simple past for a finished time range.

items.prompt: Air pollution in the capital has ______ (rise) sharply since 2010.
items.reason: present perfect (has risen); rise is intransitive, so no object.

items.prompt: Governments should invest more heavily ______ public transport.
items.reason: invest in.

items.prompt: Smallpox was completely ______ (eradicate) by the end of the 1970s.
items.reason: passive voice needs was + V3.

items.prompt: Automation may ______ (undermine) job security in several sectors.
items.reason: the base form follows the modal may.

items.prompt: The report ______ (focus) mainly on youth unemployment.
items.reason: present simple, third person singular (the report focuses on).

items.prompt: By 2020, the jobless rate had ______ (fall) to a record low.
items.reason: past perfect needs had + V3; fall is irregular (fell, fallen).

items.prompt: Tourism contributes significantly ______ the local economy.
items.reason: contribute to.

items.prompt: Strict penalties can ______ (deter) people ______ committing crimes.
items.reason: base form after can; the structure is deter someone from doing.

items.prompt: The company has been ______ (invest) heavily in renewable technology.
items.reason: present perfect continuous needs has been + V4.

items.prompt: Chronic water shortages often result ______ poor long-term planning.
items.reason: result from points to a cause; result in points to a consequence.

items.prompt: Renewable sources are gradually ______ (replace) fossil fuels.
items.reason: present continuous needs are + V4.

items.prompt: The new curriculum is ______ (design) to ______ (enhance) critical thinking.
items.reason: passive is designed; base form after to.

items.prompt: Coastal communities must ______ (adapt) ______ rising sea levels.
items.reason: base form after must; adapt to.

items.prompt: Over the last century, average temperatures have ______ (rise) steadily.
items.reason: present perfect (have risen).

items.prompt: The charity has ______ (provide) thousands of families ______ clean water.
items.reason: present perfect has provided; provide someone with something.

blocks.title: Exercise 3.2 · Cohesive Device Transformation
blocks.instructions: The paragraph below is written at roughly Band 6.0. Its ideas are sound, but the sentences are short and joined only by basic connectors. Rewrite it as one connected Band 8.0 to 9.0 paragraph, using higher-level cohesive devices accurately and varying them. Do not add new ideas; improve only the linking and flow.

items.prompt: Online education has become very popular. It is cheaper than traditional classes. Students can also study from home. But it has some problems. There is less interaction with teachers. Also, many students lack self-discipline. So, a lot of them do not finish their courses. Online education is useful. But it cannot fully replace the classroom.
items.answer: Online education has grown enormously in popularity, largely because it is cheaper than traditional classes and allows students to study from home. Notwithstanding these advantages, it carries certain drawbacks. To begin with, there is far less interaction with teachers. Moreover, many learners lack the self-discipline that independent study demands; consequently, a significant proportion fail to complete their courses. Online education is therefore undeniably useful, yet it cannot fully replace the classroom.
items.reason: because correctly introduces a full clause, while Notwithstanding is correctly followed by a noun phrase (these advantages), not a clause; the semicolon before consequently joins two related clauses; no device is repeated, so the cohesion is varied rather than mechanical.
